subject: Post-call recap — buying committee checklist, eval rubric, legal on-ramp
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Claire Zhang <c.zhang@novamed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jul 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — buying committee checklist, eval rubric, legal on-ramp

Hi Claire — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps to keep momentum: 

Call highlights
- Primary use case: triaging clinician notes and extracting discrete problem list items for EHR sync.
- Target outcome: 50% reduction in manual chart review time; accuracy threshold: >=92% on key entities.
- Timeline: pilot starting Sept 1, production pilot (3 months) then evaluate for enterprise rollout.

Stakeholders (as discussed) — please confirm:
- Economic buyer: Michael Torres (CTO) — is that still correct?
- Procurement: procurement@novamed.com (we talked about NDA first)
- Security/contact for DPA: who owns privacy/security reviews?

Short-term asks (to accelerate contracting):
1) Please confirm the buying committee roster (names + roles).
2) Can you route the NDA to procurement/security for e-sign? I attached our standard NDA as a starting point.
3) Share any required compliance artifacts (SOC 2 scope, data retention policy) so Ben can line up the right contacts.

Proposed legal routing sequence (we recommend): NDA -> DPA -> MSA (redlines only on DPA/MSA; NDA is usually quick). Typical internal turn-times we see: NDA 1-3 business days, DPA review 3-7 days, MSA redline 5-10 days depending on legal bandwidth. Ben (cc'd) will own the DPA/MSA sequencing from Redwood's side.

Next operational steps:
- I'll send a short mutual action plan draft by EOD that maps owners and dates.
- Ben will attach a concise playbook for procurement: required artifacts, suggested SOW language, and turnaround SLAs.

If that plan looks good, let me know the best email to send the NDA for signature (DocuSign or procurement portal).

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
<aisha@redwood.com>

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Claire Zhang <c.zhang@novamed.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jul 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood legal & procurement playbook — sequencing and SLAs

Claire / Aisha — looping in the legal playbook and what I recommend for sequencing so everyone has expectations. Short version at the top, details below.

TL;DR (recommended sequence)
1) NDA (DocuSign) — owner: Novamed procurement; Redwood turnaround: 1 business day for minor edits.
2) Security intake / DPA scoping — owner: Raj Patel (Novamed); Redwood: provide DPA template + SOC 2 scope within 2 business days.
3) DPA review & redlines — owner: Novamed legal/security; Redwood legal will respond to redlines within 3 business days for typical requests.
4) MSA / commercial terms — owner: Novamed legal & economic buyer; Redwood legal will propose final MSA within 5 business days of DPA alignment.

Recommended owners on Redwood side: Aisha (commercial owner), Ben (legal/commercial coordination), Redwood Security (sec@redwood.com) for technical artifacts.

Attachments I will send now: 
- Novamed_RFI_answers_v1.xlsx: quick answers to your questionnaire where we map controls to SOC 2 and data handling.
- Redwood_sample_DPA_v1.docx: our standard DPA (we'll tailor to your needs).

Turn-times & redline guidance (empirical):
- NDA: 1-3 business days (we usually accept procurement edits).
- DPA: 3-7 business days per round depending on scope; most customers resolve in 1-2 rounds.
- MSA: 5-10 business days once DPA language is agreed; if there are unusual commercial asks it can take longer.

If Novamed prefers, we can do a 30-minute legal sync with Raj + Redwood security to walk through the DPA and SOC 2 artifacts; that often reduces total calendar time. Let me know availability.

Ben Carter
Head of Legal Operations (Sales) | Redwood Inference
<ben@redwood.com>
